title: Canonical nested-cutoff comparison on one column
statement:
Let C be abelian and L a nonnegative cochain complex. For integers a<=b, let g between the cutoffs be compatible with their inclusions into the reextended L. Every map q from cokernel(g) to the smart window whose composite with the cokernel projection equals the restricted b-1 upper truncation of the canonical lower projection at a is a quasi-isomorphism. The projection equation, rather than just the type of q, is essential. theorem verticalCutoff_column_quasiIso
    (L : CochainComplex C ℕ) (a b : ℤ) (hab : a ≤ b)
    (g : (verticalCutoff a).obj L ⟶ (verticalCutoff b).obj L)
    (hg : g ≫ (verticalCutoffι b).app L = (verticalCutoffι a).app L)
    (q : cokernel g ⟶ (verticalWindow a b).obj L)
    (hq : cokernel.π g ≫ q = HomologicalComplex.restrictionMap
      (CochainComplex.truncLEMap
        (CochainComplex.πTruncGE (L.extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) a) (b - 1))
      ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat) : QuasiIso q

source.place: Section Truncations, tag 0118, canonical cochain truncations; see also Mathlib Algebra/Homology/Embedding/AreComplementary.lean, shortComplexTruncLEX₃ToTruncGE. Nested-cutoff kernel argument written by C2.

proof.text: Monicity determines the nested cutoff map. The projection equation determines q uniquely by the cokernel universal property. Identify its degreewise kernel with the two-term image complex at a-1,a. Its differential is the canonical image isomorphism, so the kernel is contractible, and the short exact homology sequence proves QuasiIso. If a=b or b<=0 both objects vanish; if a<0 the lower projection is an isomorphism; if a=0 the image in degree -1 is zero, so restriction retains the whole nonzero kernel.
